_note: Week of June 1–7, 2026. Mediterranean T2D. 190lb 67M lightly active, retired, enjoys cooking. ~1900 kcal, ~135g protein, ~115g low-GI carbs, ~88g fat, 32g+ fiber. Every day is a different meal. No raw onion. Bedtime snack every night. Addressed to 'you' throughout.

breakfasts.name: Mediterranean Yogurt Bowl
breakfasts.note: A solid week-starter. The walnuts and flaxseed slow down the berry sugars so you get a steady morning instead of a spike-and-crash.
steps: Thaw berries overnight in the fridge or microwave 45 sec.
Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Top with berries, walnuts, flaxseed, chia seeds.
No sweetener needed — the berries do the work.

breakfasts.name: Two-Egg Scramble with Spinach & Feta
breakfasts.note: Low-carb Tuesday — no bread today. Eggs and olive oil carry the morning. The feta adds a salty, creamy finish that makes this feel like more than a quick scramble.
steps: Heat olive oil in a small non-stick pan over medium.
Add spinach and tomatoes, stir 1 min until spinach wilts.
Crack in eggs, scramble gently until just set.
Season with oregano and salt. Slide onto plate, crumble feta on top.

breakfasts.name: Almond Butter Toast with Chia
breakfasts.note: Simple and satisfying. The almond butter fat slows down the toast carbs so you don't feel it. Good morning for getting Wednesday's batch cooking done while you eat.

ingredients.item: Apple — 1 medium, sliced on the side

steps: Toast bread. Spread almond butter generously.
Sprinkle flaxseed and chia seeds over the top.
Eat with sliced apple on the side — but eat the toast first, apple after.

breakfasts.name: Sardine Toast with Lemon & Cucumber
breakfasts.note: Worth trying if you haven't done sardines at breakfast — it's very common in Mediterranean countries. High omega-3, high protein, almost no carb impact. The lemon and cucumber freshen it up completely.

ingredients.item: Sardines in olive oil — 1/2 can (~50g), drained

steps: Toast the bread.
Lay cucumber rounds on top. Fork the sardines over the cucumber.
Squeeze lemon juice over everything. Crack black pepper, pinch of oregano.
Eat open-faced.

breakfasts.name: Greek Egg & Veggie Bake (2 servings — eat half now, save half)
breakfasts.note: Takes about 25 minutes but makes two servings — eat one now, refrigerate one for a quick future breakfast or lunch. Good Friday project if you have a slow morning.

ingredients.item: Dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Heat olive oil in a small oven-safe skillet over medium.
Add tomatoes, pepper, spinach — cook 3 min until softened. Season with oregano, garlic powder, salt.
Crack in 4 eggs evenly over the vegetables. Scatter feta and olives on top.
Transfer pan to oven. Bake 12–14 min until whites are set but yolks are still slightly soft.
Cut in half — eat one half now, cover and refrigerate the other.

breakfasts.name: Walnut & Berry Overnight Oats
breakfasts.note: Make these Friday night before bed — they're ready when you wake up. Oats are rolled, not instant, which gives a much lower GI. The walnuts and flaxseed keep the carb absorption slow.

ingredients.item: Frozen mixed berries — 1/4 cup (add in the morning)
Water or unsweetened almond milk — 1/3 cup

steps: Friday night: combine oats, yogurt, chia, flaxseed, and liquid in a jar or container. Stir well, seal, refrigerate overnight.
Saturday morning: stir, top with berries and walnuts.
Eat cold — no heating needed. Add a splash more liquid if too thick.

breakfasts.name: Full Mediterranean Egg Plate
breakfasts.note: Sunday deserves a proper breakfast. This is modeled after a Turkish-style morning spread — eggs, olives, tomatoes, cucumber, a little cheese, good bread. Takes 15 minutes and feels like a real sit-down.

ingredients.item: Eggs — 2 large, soft-boiled or fried in olive oil

steps: Soft-boil eggs: bring water to boil, lower eggs in, cook 7 min, transfer to cold water 1 min, peel. OR fry in olive oil over medium-low until whites set.
Toast bread.
Arrange everything on a plate: eggs, tomatoes, cucumber rounds, olives, feta crumbled over.
Drizzle a little olive oil over the vegetables. Season with oregano, salt, pepper.
Eat slowly — it's Sunday.

lunches.name: Chickpea & Spinach Bowl with Lemon-Olive Oil Dressing
lunches.note: Fast to put together if you prepped on Sunday. Chickpeas are filling and low-GI — you won't be hungry before dinner.

ingredients.item: Garbanzo beans — 1/2 can (~200g), drained and rinsed

steps: Rinse chickpeas, halve tomatoes, dice cucumber.
Build the bowl: spinach base, then chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, olives, feta.
Whisk olive oil + lemon + oregano + salt in a small bowl. Pour over and toss.

lunches.name: Grilled Chicken over Lentil Soup
lunches.note: Lentils have one of the lowest glycemic indexes of any food — around 32. A bowl of this at lunch sets you up for steady blood sugar all afternoon.

ingredients.item: Lentils (dry green) — 45g dry (or use Sunday batch)

steps: If using Sunday batch: reheat one lentil portion in a pot or microwave.
Season chicken with olive oil, lemon, paprika, salt. Pan-sear 5–6 min per side over medium-high, or bake 400°F for 22 min.
Slice chicken, lay on top of hot lentil soup. A drizzle of olive oil to finish.

lunches.name: Tuna-Stuffed Avocado with Cherry Tomatoes
lunches.note: No cooking required. Avocado replaces any grain here and gives you the healthy fat that keeps you full. Good for a lighter midday when Wednesday dinner is more substantial.

ingredients.item: Canned tuna in water — 1 can (142g), drained well

steps: Drain tuna thoroughly. Mix with lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper.
Dice some tomatoes and cucumber into the tuna mix.
Halve the avocado, remove pit. Scoop a little extra avocado from each half to make room.
Fill each half with tuna mixture. Pile the remaining tomatoes around the plate.

lunches.name: White Bean & Roasted Pepper Salad
lunches.note: Roasted peppers from a jar work great here — no raw onion, and the sweet smokiness pairs perfectly with cannellini beans and good olive oil. This is a very Mediterranean combination.

ingredients.item: Fresh or dried basil, salt, pepper

steps: Drain and rinse beans. Drain and slice roasted peppers.
Toss spinach, beans, peppers, tomatoes, olives together in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil + lemon juice + basil + salt. Top with crumbled feta.

lunches.name: Leftover Greek Egg Bake (from Friday breakfast) or Quick Sardine Plate
lunches.note: If you saved the other half of Friday's egg bake — this is it. Eat it cold or warm it in a pan 3 min. If you finished it, the sardine plate below takes 5 minutes.

ingredients.item: Leftover egg bake (1/2 portion from Friday breakfast)
OR: Sardines in olive oil — 1 can, drained
Whole grain bread — 1 slice, toasted (sardine option)

steps: Egg bake option: warm in a non-stick pan over medium-low for 3 min, covered. Eat with sliced cucumber and tomatoes on the side.
Sardine option: toast bread, lay sardines on top with lemon juice and oregano. Cucumber and tomatoes on the side dressed with olive oil + salt.

lunches.name: Lentil & Feta Salad with Walnuts
lunches.note: A more textured salad — lentils, walnuts, feta, bright dressing. Works great at room temperature so you don't need to reheat anything. Good Saturday lunch before a more relaxed dinner.

ingredients.item: Lentils (dry green) — 50g dry, cooked and cooled

steps: Cook lentils: 50g dry + 250ml water, simmer 20 min. Drain, spread on a plate to cool 10 min.
Combine cooled lentils with spinach, tomatoes, cucumber in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil + lemon + cumin + oregano + salt. Toss.
Top with crumbled feta and walnuts.

lunches.name: Hummus & Chicken Plate with Warm Pita
lunches.note: A generous Sunday spread. Slice some leftover chicken, or quickly grill a fresh piece. The hummus, pita, and veggies make it feel like a proper sit-down meal without a lot of dishes.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast — 150g, grilled or from Sunday dinner batch
Whole wheat pita — 1 pita, warmed and torn

steps: Warm pita: 30 sec per side in a dry pan, or wrap in foil and warm in oven 5 min.
Spread hummus on a plate, drizzle with olive oil, dust with paprika.
Arrange sliced chicken, tomatoes, cucumber, olives around the plate.
Tear pita into pieces for dipping. Squeeze lemon over everything.

dinners.name: Baked Salmon with Roasted Zucchini & Small Quinoa
dinners.note: Classic Mediterranean opener. Salmon's omega-3s are especially valuable for managing blood sugar and cardiovascular health. Keeping quinoa to 35g dry — just enough carb at dinner to stabilize overnight.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, paprika, dried oregano, salt

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss zucchini in 1 tbsp olive oil + salt. Spread on a baking sheet.
Place salmon on same sheet. Drizzle with remaining olive oil + lemon + garlic powder + paprika + oregano.
Roast 18–20 min until salmon flakes easily and zucchini edges are golden.
While roasting: rinse quinoa, simmer in 70ml water 15 min, fluff.
Plate: small quinoa mound, salmon on top, zucchini alongside. Extra lemon over everything.

dinners.name: Chicken Thighs with Roasted Peppers & Olives (No Grain)
dinners.note: No grain tonight — extra olive oil and the thighs provide the fat calories. Everything goes on one pan. The pan juices are good — spoon them over at the end.

ingredients.item: Dried oregano, thyme, garlic powder, salt

steps: Marinate chicken in 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon + oregano + thyme + garlic powder — 20 min minimum, overnight is better.
Toss peppers and tomatoes in remaining olive oil + salt. Spread on a sheet pan.
Nestle chicken among the vegetables. Bake at 425°F for 25–28 min until chicken hits 165°F.
Add olives to the pan in the last 5 min.
Spoon the pan juices over everything before serving.

dinners.name: White Bean & Tomato Skillet with Cod
dinners.note: One pan, almost no cleanup. Cannellini beans and tomatoes simmer into a thick sauce, then you nestle the cod right in to poach. Very Italian coastal — this is the kind of thing you'd get in a trattoria in Liguria.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, salt

steps: Thaw cod in cold water 20 min, pat dry.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium. Add garlic powder + oregano + red pepper flakes, stir 30 sec.
Add tomatoes and cannellini beans. Simmer 5 min, season with salt.
Nestle cod into the sauce. Cover and cook 8–10 min until it flakes easily.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Finish with lemon.
Serve straight from the pan.

dinners.name: Turkey & Lentil Stuffed Bell Peppers
dinners.note: Lentils inside the stuffing bulk the filling while adding fiber and slow carbs — you need less meat and the result is more satisfying. The feta on top melts into a salty golden crust.

ingredients.item: Bell peppers — 2 large, halved lengthwise, seeds removed
Garlic powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt

steps: Cook lentils: 40g dry + 200ml water, simmer 18–20 min until just tender. Drain.
Cut peppers in half lengthwise, remove seeds. Brush lightly with olive oil. Set on a baking sheet cut-side up.
Brown turkey in a pan over medium-high. Season well. Mix in cooked lentils + tomatoes + spices. Simmer 5 min.
Fill pepper halves with the turkey-lentil mixture. Crumble feta on top.
Bake at 375°F for 30 min until peppers are tender and feta is golden.

dinners.name: Shrimp with Chickpeas & Roasted Eggplant
dinners.note: End-of-week dinner that's quick and lighter on the cooking. Shrimp cooks in under 5 minutes. The eggplant roasts while you prep everything else — it gets almost meaty when done right.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, salt

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss eggplant + chickpeas + tomatoes in 1.5 tbsp olive oil + garlic powder + paprika + salt.
Spread on a large sheet pan. Roast 22 min, toss once at 12 min.
Meanwhile toss shrimp with remaining olive oil + cumin + paprika + salt.
When eggplant is done, push to the sides. Add shrimp to center of pan.
Roast another 5–6 min until shrimp are pink and curled.
Squeeze lemon over everything. Toss lightly and serve from the pan.

dinners.name: Sardine Puttanesca over Lentils
dinners.note: A Saturday project worth making. Puttanesca (tomatoes, olives, capers, herbs) is bold enough to make sardines taste genuinely great — this is the sauce that converts people. Lentils instead of pasta keep the carbs low and the GI very manageable.

ingredients.item: Sardines in olive oil — 1 can (~100g), drained

substitutions.item: Canned tuna in water — 2 cans (drain well)
substitutions.note: Lower omega-3 but works great in this sauce.
substitutions.shopping: Canned tuna in water — 2 cans (sardine swap, Sat)

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, red pepper flakes, dried oregano, salt

steps: Cook lentils: 55g dry + 275ml water, simmer 20 min until tender. Drain, season with salt.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium. Add garlic powder + red pepper flakes + oregano, stir 30 sec.
Add tomatoes + olives + capers. Simmer 8–10 min until slightly thickened.
Open sardines, break into large chunks. Nestle into sauce. Heat through 2 min — don't stir too much.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Squeeze in lemon.
Spoon sauce over lentils.

dinners.name: Greek Baked Chicken with Roasted Vegetables & Hummus
dinners.note: Sunday dinner that also sets up the week. While the chicken and vegetables roast, get the lentil soup going on the stove for next week's lunches. The hummus and pita make this feel like a proper spread.

ingredients.item: Dried oregano, garlic powder, paprika, salt

steps: Marinate chicken in 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon + oregano + garlic powder + paprika — 30 min.
Toss vegetables in remaining olive oil + salt. Add to sheet pan with chicken.
Bake at 425°F for 25 min until chicken is 165°F and vegetables are roasted and slightly charred.
START BATCH COOK WHILE THIS BAKES: Put on a pot of lentil soup for next week (lentils + canned tomatoes + water + cumin + paprika + spinach, 30 min simmer). Hard-boil 4 eggs for bedtime snacks.
Warm pita half 30 sec in a dry pan. Plate chicken + vegetables. Hummus on the side.
Portion leftover lentil soup into 4 containers once cool.

daytimeSnacks.name: Hummus with Cucumber & Bell Pepper
daytimeSnacks.desc: 4 tbsp hummus with cucumber rounds and bell pepper strips. Classic, filling, zero blood sugar impact worth worrying about.

daytimeSnacks.name: Walnuts & Hard Boiled Egg
daytimeSnacks.desc: 14g walnuts and 1 hard boiled egg. High fat, moderate protein, nearly zero carb. Good on a low-carb morning like Tuesday.

daytimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt with Chia Seeds
daytimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 1 tbsp chia seeds. Stir together, let sit 5 min to gel. High protein, very low sugar impact.

daytimeSnacks.name: Almonds & Apple
daytimeSnacks.desc: 28g almonds (~23 almonds) with 1 medium apple. The fat in the almonds slows the apple's sugar down. Eat the almonds first.

daytimeSnacks.name: Sardines on Half a Pita
daytimeSnacks.desc: Half a can of sardines on half a whole wheat pita with lemon juice and black pepper. Good Friday afternoon fuel before a lighter dinner.

daytimeSnacks.name: Feta, Olives & Cherry Tomatoes
daytimeSnacks.desc: 30g feta, 10 kalamata olives, a handful of cherry tomatoes. Olive oil and a pinch of oregano if you want. Zero cooking, very Mediterranean.

daytimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter & Celery Sticks
daytimeSnacks.desc: 2 tbsp almond butter with celery sticks for dipping. Good Sunday afternoon snack while the batch cooking is going.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter on Whole Grain Toast
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: The fat in almond butter slows digestion of the toast carbs, releasing glucose gradually over 4–6 hours. This gives your liver something to work with overnight without any blood sugar spike going to bed.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 slice whole grain toast + 2 tbsp almond butter. No honey, no fruit on top. Eat slowly.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt & Walnuts
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Protein digests slowly and can help prevent your liver from releasing excess glucose overnight. The walnuts add fat to slow things further. Research in T2D patients has linked a Greek yogurt bedtime snack to improved fasting glucose.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 14g walnuts. Stir together or eat the walnuts on the side.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Hard Boiled Egg & Almonds
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Almost pure fat and protein — virtually no glucose impact. Good option after a higher-carb dinner, or if you want something savory. The small carb from almonds is just enough to prevent lows without any spike.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 hard boiled egg (from the Sunday batch) + 28g almonds. Salt the egg.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Small Bowl of Lentil Soup
bedtimeSnacks.timing: 45–60 min before bed (gives more time to digest)
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Lentils have a glycemic index around 32 — one of the lowest of any carb source. They digest so slowly they effectively act as a timed-release glucose drip overnight. Particularly good after a lighter dinner.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: About 3/4 cup of the batch-cooked lentil soup, reheated. Add a drizzle of olive oil.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter & Celery
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: High fat, moderate protein, very low carb. Good end-of-week option — satisfying without being heavy. The almond butter fat keeps things stable through the night.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 2 tbsp almond butter with 3–4 celery sticks. Simple and quick.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt with Chia Seeds & Walnuts
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Protein plus fat plus the fiber from chia seeds — everything slows digestion and keeps blood sugar from dropping overnight. This combination is particularly good for sleep quality.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 1 tbsp chia seeds + 14g walnuts. Stir and eat.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Whole Grain Toast with Almond Butter & Flaxseed
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Same principle as Monday — fat slows carb absorption for a long overnight release. The flaxseed adds extra fiber and omega-3s. A good weekly bookend to how you started Monday.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 slice whole grain toast + 2 tbsp almond butter + 1 tbsp ground flaxseed sprinkled on top.

Produce: Baby spinach — 1 large bag (used almost every day)
Bell peppers — 6 total, mixed colors (Tue dinner + Thu dinner stuffing + Thu lunch + Sun dinner + Fri breakfast bake)
Celery — 1 bunch (Sun snack + Fri bedtime snack)
Meat, Fish & Seafood: Sardines in olive oil — 4 cans (Thu breakfast + Fri snack + Sat dinner + backup)
Chicken breast — ~650g total (Tue lunch + Sun lunch + Sun dinner + batch cook)
Canned tuna in water — 2 cans (Wed lunch)
Dairy & Eggs: Plain nonfat Greek yogurt — 8 containers (Mon breakfast + Wed snack + Sat breakfast + Tue/Sat/Sun bedtime snack + extra)
Eggs — 1 dozen (Tue breakfast + Fri breakfast bake + bedtime snack batch)
Canned & Jarred: Garbanzo beans (chickpeas) — 3 cans (Mon lunch + Fri dinner + Sun lunch)
Cannellini beans — 2 cans (Wed dinner + Thu lunch)
Lentils, dry green — 400g bag (Tue/Sat lunch + Thu dinner + Sat dinner + Sun batch soup)
Diced tomatoes — 5 cans (batch soup + Wed dinner + Thu dinner + Sat dinner)
Jarred roasted red peppers — 1 jar (Thu lunch)
Kalamata olives — 1 large jar (used throughout the week)
Hummus — 1 large container (~400g) (Thu lunch + Sun lunch + Sun dinner + Mon snack)
Sardines in olive oil — see Meat & Fish above
Bread, Grains & Nuts: Whole grain bread — 1 loaf (Thu breakfast + Wed breakfast + Fri snack + bedtime snacks Mon/Sun)
Whole wheat pita — 1 pack (Fri snack + Sun dinner + Sun lunch)
Rolled oats (not instant) — small bag (Sat breakfast)
Quinoa, dry — small bag (Mon dinner, need ~35g)
Almonds — 1 bag (~200g) (Thu snack + Wed bedtime + Sun bedtime)
Walnuts — 1 bag (~200g) (Mon breakfast + Tue snack + Sat breakfast + Tue/Sat bedtime snacks)
Almond butter — 1 jar (Wed breakfast + Sun snack + Mon/Fri/Sun bedtime snacks)
Pantry & Condiments: Olive oil — 1 bottle (used heavily every day)
Ground flaxseed — 1 bag (Mon/Wed breakfast + Sun bedtime snack)
Chia seeds — 1 bag (Mon/Wed/Sat breakfast + Wed snack + Sat bedtime snack)
Dried oregano — used almost every meal
Garlic powder — used almost every meal
Red pepper flakes — Wed dinner + Sat dinner
